Confirmed via the incident data itself: 77 literal searches for mechanically-generated, nonexistent names (useReactQueryCancelProvider, useReactQueryAbort, useReactQuerySkeleton, and ~57 more combinatorial useReactQuery* / React-Query-ecosystem / bare-React-hook names) found zero matches, as expected -- none of those identifiers exist anywhere in this codebase.

One wildcard regex search using only the task's own domain keyword ('voucher'), with no exact hook name known in advance -- grep -rniE 'use\w*voucher\w*(query|mutation)' against the services directory -- found all 5 real hooks in a single call: useGetVouchersQuery, useGetVoucherQuery, useCreateVoucherMutation, usePostVoucherMutation, useCancelVoucherMutation. This directly proves authoritative discovery was available via the SAME search_files tool the member called 77 times with literal guesses -- the gap was search STRATEGY (sequential literal guessing instead of a wildcard/regex pattern), not a tooling capability gap.

An even more generic regex matching the file's own export-list line shape (^\s*use[A-Z]\w*(Query|Mutation),?\s*$), with NO domain keyword at all, found every hook export in the file in one call, including all 5 voucher hooks -- confirms the discovery method is robust even without knowing the module name in advance, not just a lucky keyword match.

60 distinct patterns across 77 total search calls (per the T37 incident's own extractor.search_patterns/counts.searches) implies roughly 17 calls were repeats of already-tried patterns within that one delegation. Separately, confirmed via code reading that a FRESH delegation to the same member carries no memory of which negative results a PRIOR delegation already established -- so if the Researcher had been delegated to again for the same hooks question, it would have had no record of the 60 names already proven absent and could repeat the same guesses. Not observed directly in this specific incident (seq 3 was delegated to only once for this objective), but a real, evidenced risk for the general case.
